productionReference: WindowsLinker.CompilePartitioned uses Math.Max(1, Environment.ProcessorCount) before NativeJobLimit and partition sizing.
decisions: Nonempty DOTNET_PROCESSOR_COUNT precedes COMPlus_PROCESSOR_COUNT; parse a decimal unsigned Windows DWORD prefix, accept override only in 1..65535. Zero, malformed and out-of-range values use OS availability.

CPU group availability and configured GC/thread use-all-groups choose all active processors; otherwise count current process affinity bits, preserving the reference failure=1 and zero-mask=64 decisions.

A successful CPU-rate job query applies enabled hard cap or min/max maximum rate, rounds processors*rate/10000 upward and clamps availability. Explicit processor count overrides both affinity and quota.

Keep raw Win32 ABI calls in a private compiler-host runtime adapter. Native Text is not an ABI-safe C input: use an explicit checked DWORD numeric-prefix parser and query Windows NLS C1_SPACE via GetStringTypeW, which matches all30 current CSharp Unicode observations including legacy U+180E. Never substitute the configured/capped compute pool count.

Record the selected managed runtime configuration. It has no AppContext CPU-group overrides. Multiple-group hardware and cross-host Linux query remain unverified; do not claim them from this one-group Windows proof.
